_comment: Hand-authored. The HUD's number printers and the life meter, bank 7 $E169-$E3F8 and $E406-$E423. The generator for 20-traced.json subtracts these.

regions.name: HUD: the AREA, X and Y line
regions.description: Row 27 of the HUD (PPU $2766-$2770; the word AREA is the inline string at $E162). Prints the area number - $50 in the labyrinth, $51 when $30 bit 1 is set (a TGL game) - through the 3-digit printer $E1D3, then the map column $52 at $276B and the row $53 at $276F, each with the letter X or Y ($58, $59) written over the hundreds cell of the printed number (so a value of 255 shows as X55). It is entered by FALLING THROUGH from $E15F, which queues the label with the inline-string call $D576; $E15F is called when a room or stage is set up (for example $EB1D). RUN with several values: row 27 read '..AREA..9..X.3.Y17..', '..AREA.10..X55.Y.0..' and, in a TGL game, the corridor number in the area slot.

regions.name: Split a byte into decimal digits
regions.description: In: A. Out: $10 = hundreds, $11 = tens, A = ones. Subtracts 100 and then 10 repeatedly (a loop of SBC/INC, restoring the last overshoot). Preserves Y in $12. Used by the 3-digit printer.

regions.name: HUD: the uses left of the selected weapon
regions.description: Slot $C072. Prints $3E - the uses left (chips / cost) - as three right-aligned digits at PPU $2739 (row 25, after the word SHOT) and commits the queue entry. Called by the weapon cursor code at $FD08. RUN: $3E = 37 gave 'T 37', 0 gave 'T  0', 255 gave 'T255'.

regions.name: Queue a 3-digit number, leading zeros blanked
regions.description: In: A = the value, $19:$18 = the PPU address. Reserves 6 bytes of the PPU queue ($D6D3 waits for room, $D6E0 reserves), splits A through $E1A3, and builds [3][hi][lo][hundreds][tens][ones] at $0100 + the cursor: digits are $30 + the value, and a zero hundreds or tens cell becomes $20 (blank). It does NOT commit the entry - the callers do ($D6F7). Call sites: the X and Y numbers ($E187, $E198), the shared tail $E1CD used by the area number and the shots-left number, and the life meter's number ($E36C).

regions.name: Chip tier, then point the number printer at the chip counter
regions.description: Slot $C05A; also called from $FD0B after the weapon cursor moves. Copies the chips $4C/$4D to $16/$17 and sets the main gun's tier $3A: 0 under 100, 1 for 100-199, 2 for 200-2,047 and 3 from 2,048 (by the high byte $17: 8 or more means 2,048 and over, tier 3; any other non-zero high byte, 256-2,047, tier 2). Then sets $18/$19 = PPU $272F (row 25, after the word CHIP) and FALLS INTO the number printer at $E24B, so every change of the chip total redraws the counter and re-derives the tier in one call. RUN with 15 values: tier 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3 ... at 7, 85, 99, 100, 199, 200, 1185, 2047, 2048.

regions.name: Print a 16-bit number: up to four digits, capped at 9999
regions.description: Slot $C04E. In: $17:$16 = the value, $19:$18 = the PPU address. Reserves a 7-byte queue entry [4][hi][lo] + 4 cells (initially '0', '0', ' ', ' ') and builds the digits by repeated subtraction: thousands (up to ten subtractions of 1,000: if all ten succeed, the value is 10,000 or more, the digit cells are set to 9 and the routine ends - so everything from 10,000 up shows 9999), hundreds (100), tens (10) and ones, blanking leading zeros: the digits are left-justified by shifting the write position (INX) when a leading zero is dropped, and the unused cells at the right stay blank (a one-digit value sits one cell in: ' 7  '). The same routine prints the shop's prices above the items (bank 2 $851B). RUN on the chip counter with 0, 7, 85, 99, 100, 199, 200, 1185, 2047, 2048, 9999, 10000, 12345, 40000, 65535: the row read '.0..', '.7..', '.85.', '.99.', '.100', '.199', '.200', '1185', '2047', '2048', '9999' and 9999 for everything larger.

regions.name: HUD: the life meter - step the shown value, redraw only what changed
regions.description: Called first thing every frame by the HUD routine $E0F9. $49 is the SHOWN life, $48 the real one; when they differ the shown value moves one unit toward it per frame (decrease when $49 >= $48, step -1; else +1), so the bar drains and fills visibly. The bar is made of 8-pixel tiles: the tile count is ((value - 1) / 8) + 1 ($15 old, $17 new) and the fill of the last tile is (value - 1) AND 7 ($16). Within one tile only the partial tile changes (the entry at $E3CC); when the value crosses a tile boundary it queues (a) the number and the life icon: the tile COUNT, not the life, as up to three digits at PPU $2740 with tile $23 written in the cell before the first digit ($E357-$E37C); (b) the new last tile as tile $FF, the special partial tile, at bar position $17 (PPU $2742 + position, through $E406); (c) the old last tile, now $22 (empty) when draining or $21 (full) when filling. If the queue lacks room it gives up and the shown value stays, so the redraw is retried next frame. $E3CC queues 5 bytes for PPU $1FF9 - plane 1, rows 1-5 of tile $FF in pattern table 1 - each the fill mask for the last tile ($E3F9[fraction]: 80 C0 E0 F0 F8 FC FE FF) ANDed with the bar's shape for that row ($E401: EE FE FF FF EE, which rounds the ends). So tile $FF's pixels are rewritten every step: the bar's partial segment is drawn by editing CHR RAM. Ends by storing the new value in $49. RUN on the corridor savestate: from 160 down to 32 and back up; row 26 read 'icon, 4, 21 21 21 FF 22 ...' at 32 and 5 at 33-37, and tile $FF's five bytes went ee fe ff ff ee (full) -> ec fc fc fc ec -> e8 f8 f8 f8 e8 -> e0 f0 f0 f0 e0 -> 80 80 80 80 80 as the value fell one pixel at a time.

regions.name: Meter: queue one bar tile
regions.description: In: A = bar position (1-24), Y = the queue cursor. Returns carry set and does nothing for 0 or 25 and over; otherwise writes [1][$27][$42 + position] at the cursor, leaves the data byte for the caller and advances Y by 4 (PPU $2743 for position 1, the first bar tile after the number). Called twice by the life meter ($E392, $E3A7) and once by $E424 ($E43A), which the score-bonus code reaches (bank 7 $DFAE) to draw the bar's new empty tile when the maximum life grows.
